name: Jallianwala Bagh
summary: Dyer marched fifty riflemen of the 9th Gurkhas, 54th Sikhs and 59th Rifles into the bagh on Baisakhi, blocked the narrow lane, and ordered fire without a warning to disperse. About 1,650 rounds were spent in some ten minutes.
story: Hunter accepted 379 identified dead. The Congress inquiry said a thousand was no exaggeration. Wagner later sat between those numbers.

casualties.note: Official wounded about 1,100; Congress wounded over 1,500. Wagner: perhaps 500–600 dead and ~2,000 casualties all told.

reports.headline: 379 identified dead
reports.excerpt: The official list stopped at 379. Indian door-to-door work had already forced it up from a lower first count.

reports.headline: A number that will not close
reports.excerpt: 379 was as high as the British were willing to go. It does not reflect the total. A working band of five to six hundred dead still leaves the wounded uncounted.

reports.headline: Jallianwala Bagh, a hundred years later
reports.excerpt: Hunter accepted 379 identified dead. The Congress inquiry said a thousand was no exaggeration. Wagner later sat between those numbers.

name: Crawling order
summary: From 19 April, any Indian who entered the lane where Miss Sherwood had been attacked had to crawl its length. Floggings were public. Martial law made a street into a lesson.

reports.headline: A street that had to be crawled
reports.excerpt: The crawling order is not a death count. It is the other half of April 1919: a city taught to move on its belly.

reports.headline: The crawling order that named a gali
reports.excerpt: From 19 April any Indian who entered the lane where Miss Sherwood had been attacked had to crawl its length. Floggings were public.

reports.headline: The crawling lane
reports.excerpt: Dyer’s own language was ‘on all fours’. The Congress inquiry said on the belly, like a reptile. Hunter later called the order indefensible.

name: Qissa Khwani Bazaar
summary: Armoured cars entered the bazaar. A despatch rider was killed. Fire was opened on a crowd that included Khudai Khidmatgars pledged to non-violence. Official dead 20–30; Congress 125; local lists hundreds.

reports.headline: A named list of 125
reports.excerpt: The Congress list has names. The official count has a floor. The bazaar has a memory that is larger than both.

reports.headline: Qissa Khwani Bazaar, and a named list of 125
reports.excerpt: Armoured cars entered the bazaar on 23 April 1930. Official dead 20–30; Congress 125; local lists hundreds. The Khudai Khidmatgars had pledged not to hit back.

name: Budge Budge firing
summary: Passengers of the Komagata Maru, turned from Vancouver, were ordered to a special train at Budge Budge. They refused. The police fired. Official accounts put the dead near twenty.

casualties.claimedBy: official Bengal reports and later Ghadar histories

reports.outlet: Hugh Johnston, Voyage of the Komagata Maru
reports.headline: A ship that was not allowed to land, twice
reports.excerpt: Canada turned them under a rule the empire had written. Bengal met them with a rifle at a siding.

reports.headline: What happened to the Komagata Maru passengers
reports.excerpt: Canada turned them under a rule the empire had written. Bengal met them with a rifle at a siding. Official accounts put the dead near twenty.

reports.headline: From Vancouver harbour to Budge Budge
reports.excerpt: A Japanese steamer, a continuous-journey rule, and a firing on the Hooghly. The Ghadar after is part of the same file.

name: Dandi
summary: Gandhi picked up salt on the Dandi mudflats at dawn on 6 April. The walk from Sabarmati had taken twenty-four days. The country already knew what to do with a pinch of it.

reports.outlet: Judith M. Brown, Gandhi and Civil Disobedience
reports.headline: A pinch that mapped a country
reports.excerpt: Dandi is a theatre. The raids, the pans, the pickets, and the prisons are the geography.

reports.headline: The great Dandi march, eighty years after
reports.excerpt: Gandhi picked up salt on the Dandi mudflats at dawn on 6 April. The raids, the pans, the pickets and the prisons are the geography.

reports.headline: A turning point in salt
reports.excerpt: Nehru said it seemed as though a spring had been suddenly released. Dharasana, south of Dandi, would show the state’s method.

name: Chauri Chaura
summary: A crowd burned the police station at Chauri Chaura. Twenty-two policemen died. Gandhi suspended non-cooperation. The country argued about that decision for the rest of the movement’s life.

casualties.claimedBy: official returns and later standard histories

reports.headline: A thana, a telegram, a halt
reports.excerpt: Chauri Chaura is a day the nationalist calendar cannot make simple. Amin read the peasants. Gandhi read a warning.

reports.headline: A thana, a telegram, a halt
reports.excerpt: A crowd burned the police station. Twenty-two policemen died. Gandhi suspended non-cooperation. Shahid Amin later read the peasants.

name: Quit India, Bombay
summary: The AICC had spoken at Gowalia Tank the evening before. By morning Gandhi, Nehru, Patel were in custody. Bombay and then the country went out without them.

reports.headline: A resolution, then a jail
reports.excerpt: Quit India is a speech that was arrested overnight. The movement that followed was made by people the speech had not named.

reports.headline: Quit India, when ordinary Indians took the street
reports.excerpt: The AICC had spoken at Gowalia Tank the evening before. By morning Gandhi, Nehru, Patel were in custody. Bombay went out without them.

name: Tamluk
summary: Midnapore set up a national government at Tamluk. The Raj treated it as rebellion. Matangini Hazra was among the dead at a procession. The cyclone of October 1942 and then famine sat on the same district.

casualties.note: Named dead include Matangini Hazra. District totals for Quit India firings in Midnapore are not a single agreed integer.

reports.headline: A national government in a district
reports.excerpt: Tamluk is the reminder that 1942 was not only Bombay and a jail. A subdivision tried to govern.

reports.headline: From Tamluk to a district that tried to govern
reports.excerpt: Midnapore set up a national government at Tamluk. Matangini Hazra was among the dead at a procession. The cyclone, then famine, sat on the same district.

reports.headline: India’s first people’s government, East Midnapore
reports.excerpt: The Tamralipta Jatiya Sarkar is the reminder that 1942 was not only Bombay and a jail. A subdivision tried to govern.

name: Chimur
summary: Chimur in the Central Provinces rose in mid-August 1942. Officials were killed; troops returned fire. Martial method followed. The village became a CP shorthand for Quit India.

casualties.note: Named official dead and later nationalist lists exist; no single agreed total.

reports.outlet: Central Provinces 1942 files / later local histories
reports.headline: A village the CP remembered
reports.excerpt: Chimur is a small place with a long file.

reports.headline: A village the Central Provinces remembered
reports.excerpt: Chimur rose in mid-August 1942. Officials were killed; troops returned fire. Martial method followed. Quit India had a CP shorthand.

name: Ashti
summary: Ashti, in Wardha district, is one of the 1942 villages where a crowd and a thana met, and the Raj answered with troops. It sits with Chimur in the CP list.

reports.headline: Ashti with Chimur
reports.excerpt: Two villages in the same presidency list. The method was the same.

reports.headline: Ashti with Chimur
reports.excerpt: Two villages in the same presidency list. A crowd and a thana met; the Raj answered with troops.

name: Chittagong armoury raid
summary: Surya Sen’s Indian Republican Army took the police and Auxiliary Force armouries, cut telegraph and rail, and attacked the European club. They could not hold the city. The hills took them afterwards.

casualties.sideLabel: both sides on the night of the raid
casualties.note: A handful of dead on the night; the later hunting killed more. No padded integer.

reports.headline: A city for a night
reports.excerpt: They took the weapons and could not take the town. The after was a guerrilla in the hill tracts, and a rope.

reports.headline: Surya Sen, the hero of the Chittagong uprising
reports.excerpt: They took the police and Auxiliary Force armouries on 18 April 1930 and could not hold the town. The hills took them afterwards.

name: Kakori train robbery
summary: HRA men stopped the Number 8 Down at Kakori and took the treasury chest. A passenger was killed in the firing. The conspiracy case that followed hanged Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Rajendra Lahiri and Thakur Roshan Singh.

reports.headline: A chest, a case, four hangings
reports.excerpt: The robbery is a night. The trial is the politics.

reports.headline: Remembering the martyrs of Kakori
reports.excerpt: HRA men stopped the Number 8 Down and took the treasury chest. The conspiracy case hanged Bismil, Ashfaqullah, Lahiri and Roshan Singh.

name: Bhagat Singh hanged
summary: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were hanged at Lahore Central Jail on 23 March 1931. The hanging was moved forward. The city already knew.

reports.outlet: Kama Maclean, A Revolutionary History of Interwar India
reports.headline: A calendar date
reports.excerpt: The trial had been a stage. The hanging made a year that still has a morning.

reports.headline: Bhagat Singh: the final hours
reports.excerpt: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were hanged at Lahore Central Jail on 23 March 1931. The hanging was moved forward. The city already knew.

reports.headline: Bhagat Singh
reports.excerpt: The trial had been a stage. The hanging made a calendar date that still has a morning.

name: RIN, Bombay
summary: Ratings of HMIS Talwar struck on 18 February 1946. The mutiny spread through the Bombay squadron and to other ports. City crowds came out. The Congress and the League asked the ratings to stand down.

casualties.note: City firing killed ratings and civilians; published totals vary and are not stored here as a single integer.

reports.outlet: Biswanath Bose, The Indian Naval Revolt of 1946
reports.headline: A service that struck the flag
reports.excerpt: The ratings had a list of grievances and a moment. The parties had a transfer of power to protect.

reports.headline: The 1946 Royal Indian Navy revolt
reports.excerpt: Ratings of HMIS Talwar struck on 18 February 1946. The mutiny spread through the Bombay squadron and to other ports. City crowds came out.

reports.headline: Royal Indian Navy mutiny
reports.excerpt: The Commons was told of a service that had struck the flag. The parties had a transfer of power to protect.

name: Cellular Jail opened
summary: The Cellular Jail received its first prisoners as a completed machine in 1906. Seven wings from a central tower. The Andaman penal colony was older. This building is the one the photographs kept.

reports.headline: A tower, seven wings, a sea
reports.excerpt: Kala Pani is a phrase. The jail is a plan of isolation drawn in brick.

reports.headline: How the Cellular Jail was built to isolate
reports.excerpt: Seven wings from a central tower. The Andaman penal colony was older. This building is the one the photographs kept.

reports.headline: Kala Pani, and who is named on the walls
reports.excerpt: A tower, seven wings, a sea. The jail is a plan of isolation drawn in brick.

name: Calcutta, famine peak
summary: By the autumn of 1943 the destitute of the Bengal countryside were dying in Calcutta’s streets. The Statesman published the photographs in August; the peak of starvation and then of epidemic sat in the months that followed. The province had not declared famine.

sides.label: Government of Bengal / Government of India

reports.headline: Photographs the government could not quite suppress
reports.excerpt: The camera did what the declaration of famine had not. Relief enlarged after the pictures. The countryside had already paid.

reports.headline: Three million, and the survivors still speaking
reports.excerpt: Kavita Puri’s later work sits with Sen and Maharatna: a working band of about 2.1 to 3 million excess deaths, not a single patriotic integer.

reports.headline: Churchill’s legacy, and a famine the files still argue
reports.excerpt: The province had not declared famine. The Statesman’s photographs in August 1943 did what the declaration had not.

name: Bengal famine, 1770
summary: A famine in Bengal and Bihar after the Company took the diwani. Grain still moved. The Company still collected. Hunter’s later figure of ten million dead became the traditional number; demographers treat it as an order of magnitude, not a census.

reports.outlet: W. W. Hunter, Annals of Rural Bengal
reports.headline: A third of Bengal, in a later book
reports.excerpt: Hunter popularised about ten million dead. Modern historians treat the figure as traditional and unverifiable. The disaster is real; the integer is not a register count.

name: Madras famine camps
summary: Drought from Madras through the Deccan to the Bombay Presidency, under a viceroy who would not stop grain moving to the ports. Relief was the camp and the wage. How many died depends on the historian: several million is the band.

sides.label: Rural destitute of the southern presidencies

reports.headline: Viewpoint: How British let one million Indians die in famine
reports.excerpt: Naoroji and Dutt already had the file: grain exported while the Deccan starved. Later counts for 1876–78 sit in a band of about five to 8.3 million, contested, not a census.

name: Partition of Bengal in force
summary: Curzon’s partition came into force on 16 October 1905. Swadeshi was boycott, school, bomb, and a new Muslim-majority province in the east. The map was undone at the Delhi Durbar in 1911. The communal lesson it taught was not.

reports.headline: Partition of Bengal
reports.excerpt: Announced in July 1905, in force on 16 October, annulled in December 1911. A presidency redrawn, a national method born, a communal after that outlived the map.

name: Delhi hartal firing
summary: Delhi observed Gandhi’s hartal on 30 March, a week early. After a clash over closed shops, police and troops fired on crowds near the railway station and the Clock Tower. Punjab went into a different tense; Amritsar is its own file.

casualties.claimedBy: Hunter Committee and later nationalist accounts
casualties.note: Hunter describes a short firing near the station with a handful of dead; later nationalist tallies are higher. No single agreed integer.

reports.headline: Rowlatt Acts
reports.excerpt: On 30 March, following a brawl over the closure of shops, police opened fire on a crowd of protesters in Delhi. The Act taught a country a new kind of no.

reports.headline: Why the protests began on 30 March 1919
reports.excerpt: The Rowlatt Act let the state hold a body without a court. Delhi went out first. Amritsar, two weeks later, is the massacre file.

name: Dharasana salt works
summary: After Gandhi’s arrest, Abbas Tyabji and then Sarojini Naidu led non-violent raids on the government salt depot at Dharasana. United Press correspondent Webb Miller watched men walk into steel-shod lathis without raising an arm.

casualties.claimedBy: Webb Miller’s despatch and later Congress accounts
casualties.note: Miller described fractured skulls and a ground quilted with bodies. Published death integers for the raids vary and are not stored here as a single count.

reports.headline: Marching to freedom — Webb Miller at Dharasana
reports.excerpt: Not one of the marchers even raised an arm to fend off the blows. They went down like ten-pins. In two or three minutes the ground was quilted with bodies.

reports.headline: Dandi, then the fangs of the salt depot
reports.excerpt: Dharasana, twenty-five miles south of Dandi, showed the state’s method. J. C. Kumarappa called it the fangs and claws of the government in all its ugliness.
